title: Officer fired five shots at machete wielder
article: The veteran police officer involved in Monday's fatal shooting in Port Moody fired five shots at a machete-wielding 18-year-old running toward him on a dark, dead-end street, police revealed Tuesday.
The officer killed Keyvan Tabesh of Burnaby and injured another man.
Police representative Constable Brian Soles also said Tabesh "had contact with police in the past" but was never convicted of a crime and therefore did not have a criminal record.
Soles disclosed no further details about Tabesh's past.
The Tabesh family could not be reached for comment.

According to witnesses interviewed by police, two women in a car were rammed by Tabesh's black Honda Prelude at about 2 a.m. Monday after the women left Side Pocket Billiards at Moray and St. John's in Port Moody.
Soles said police have determined it was Tabesh who got out of his car and repeatedly hit the women's car with a machete, breaking one of the windows before returning to his car and speeding away.

A few minutes later, responding to a description of the suspect vehicle, a Port Moody police officer in an unmarked car followed Tabesh's car into the 2000-block of St. George Street, which is a two-block-long dead-end street at that point.
The police officer shot Tabesh from within three metres while Tabesh brandished a machete.

Soles revealed Tuesday a total of five shots was fired by the lone officer, whom he would only identify as a former RCMP officer with more than 25 years of police experience who had been with the small municipal police department for two years.
Soles said when the unmarked police car followed Tabesh's car into the dead-end street, both cars were initially facing each other.
"At that point in time, the driver [Tabesh] was extremely upset for unknown reasons," he said. "He got out of the car and grabbed the machete as he got out, and ran towards the officer."
Soles confirmed the police officer was not in uniform.

Asked whether the officer identified himself before the shooting, Soles replied: "We believe he did. We're interviewing witnesses. There are people who think they heard things like 'stop' and 'police.'

"If you're going to speculate whether or not these kids properly understood or in fact chose not to believe this person was a police officer, the only other conclusion you have is that they got out of the car with a machete and thought they were attacking some unarmed citizen. From our perspective, it doesn't make much difference."
Police haven't released the names of the two passengers in the car, both Coquitlam residents, as charges have not been laid against them.
Soles said the passengers have given police slightly different versions of what happened that night, so police haven't yet determined whether there's evidence they committed any crimes.
One young man was shot in the pelvis area and is expected to be released from hospital within a few days. The other was arrested at the scene and later released.

After the criminal investigation has been concluded, the coroner's office will begin its investigation as inquests are required whenever a police officer is involved in the death of a suspect or a person in custody.
